items.toString:
When launching GNOME Connections using a URL via `xdg-open`, the application creates a new saved connection every time, even if the URL matches an existing one. This results in multiple duplicate entries for the same server over time.

**Steps to reproduce**:

1. Set up a desktop entry to handle `vnc://` URLs:

   ```bash
   VNC_HANDLER_DESKTOP="$HOME/.local/share/applications/gnome-connections-vnc.desktop"

   cat > "$VNC_HANDLER_DESKTOP" << 'EOF'
   [Desktop Entry]
   Name=GNOME Connections (VNC Handler)
   Comment=Connect to VNC servers via URL
   Exec=gnome-connections %u
   Icon=org.gnome.Connections
   Type=Application
   MimeType=x-scheme-handler/vnc
   NoDisplay=true
   StartupNotify=true
   EOF

   xdg-mime default gnome-connections-vnc.desktop x-scheme-handler/vnc
   ```

2. Launch a connection via:

   ```bash
   xdg-open "vnc://192.168.1.100"
   ```

3. Repeat the command.

**Expected behavior**:

* Ideally, GNOME Connections would detect an existing connection with the same URL and reuse it, or
* Provide a way to launch a **temporary connection** that is not saved persistently.

**Use case**:
This would be useful for users who launch remote sessions ad hoc (e.g. via scripts or links), without intending to save every connection.

items.fromString:
*Description*

FRR 10.4.x has a zebra bug that breaks redistribute table-direct (and ip import-table) for any route that already exists in the source kernel routing table at the moment the configuration is applied:

zebra_add_import_table_entry() clears ZEBRA_FLAG_SELECTED on the source route entry while creating the imported copy (it mutates re->flags directly instead of operating on a copy of the flags). The route walk performed for table-direct redistribution registration (zebra_redistribute()) skips entries without ZEBRA_FLAG_SELECTED, so the pre-existing route is silently never redistributed to BGP peers. A configuration reload additionally de-selects routes that were previously selected and advertised. Routes added to the table after the configuration is active are processed correctly through the live netlink path, which makes the failure timing-dependent and hard to diagnose: identical configurations work or fail depending only on whether the route predates the config.

There is no error or log message; show running-config shows correct configuration, show ip route table <N> shows the route as K *  (unselected), and show ip bgp simply lacks the prefix.

*Reproducer*

{noformat}# podman run --rm --privileged -it <frr10-based image> sh
ip link add dummy0 type dummy && ip link set dummy0 up
ip addr add 192.0.2.10/32 dev dummy0
ip route add 192.0.2.99/32 dev dummy0 table 198 proto 248   # route exists BEFORE frr starts

cat > /etc/frr/frr.conf <<'EOF'
frr defaults traditional
hostname frr-lab
ip import-table 198
router bgp 64512
 bgp router-id 192.0.2.10
 no bgp ebgp-requires-policy
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  redistribute table-direct 198 route-map RM
 exit-address-family
route-map RM permit 10
 match ip address prefix-list PL
route-map RM deny 20
ip prefix-list PL seq 10 permit 192.0.2.99/32
EOF
# daemons: zebra=yes bgpd=yes; start FRR
/usr/lib/frr/docker-start &
sleep 6
vtysh -c "show ip route table 198"   # ACTUAL: "K *" (unselected)
vtysh -c "show ip bgp"               # ACTUAL: "No BGP prefixes displayed, 0 exist"

# Control: delete and re-add the route while FRR is running
ip route del 192.0.2.99/32 table 198
ip route add 192.0.2.99/32 dev dummy0 table 198 proto 248
sleep 3
vtysh -c "show ip route table 198"   # now "K>*" (selected)
vtysh -c "show ip bgp"               # now shows *> 192.0.2.99/32 — WORKS{noformat}

*Actual result*

pre-existing route stays unselected (K * ) and is never redistributed; show ip bgp empty.


*Expected result*

the route is selected (K>*) and redistributed exactly as a route added after startup (as in the control case).

*Upstream fix*

commit b2c17ad52113b02e8b310aaef91bf74e6f1a1921 

"zebra: Do not clear selected flag on route about to be imported”

Released in FRR 10.7

Cherry-picks cleanly into frr-10.4.3

*Business impact*

OpenShift's BGP-based VIP management feature (OPNET-595) depends on exactly this pattern: kube-vip writes health-gated VIP routes into kernel table 198 and frr-k8s advertises them via redistribute table-direct 198.

The bug silently breaks VIP advertisement whenever the FRR configuration is (re)applied while a VIP route exists, taking down API/Ingress reachability with zero error signal.

OpenShift ships FRR from the frr10 RPM in the metallb-frr/frr-k8s payload image, so the fix must land in the RPM

Without this fix we are blocked and cannot ship the feature.

*Required versions*

As per [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1OPj8bm8FB0B4GgVhYSQwC_r5pjIgKtO2QfTUAhIKlFg/edit?gid=35847248#gid=35847248|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1OPj8bm8FB0B4GgVhYSQwC_r5pjIgKtO2QfTUAhIKlFg/edit?gid=35847248#gid=35847248|smart-link] , OCP 5.0 ships with RHEL 9.8 and RHEL 10.2

Ideally, both 9.8 and 10.2 get the patch.

At minimum, 10.2 gets the patch.

*Objective:* Evaluate what native metrics systemd offers, determine if they would add value to PCP users, and define the best architectural path to pull them into Performance Co-Pilot (PCP) if it makes sense to proceed.

*Key Questions to Answer:*

# What specific metrics does systemd currently expose? 
# Are some of the metrics useful for our enterprise/support use cases?
# If useful, how should they be integrated into PCP? (e.g., creating a new PMDA vs. leveraging an existing PMDA).

*Suggested Stakeholder Conversations:*

* *Upstream:* It would be good to see perspective of upstream, whether these metrics would be useful.
* *Systemd:* Consult with [~accountid:70121:8b9bc4b5-2014-4e3e-9dd4-1e807b87d002]  regarding current/future systemd metric capabilities and design alignment if needed. He already shared [https://paste.centos.org/view/03c21be1|https://paste.centos.org/view/03c21be1|smart-link]  as an example of metrics being shared by systemd.
* *Support (CEE):* Gather perspective from support ([~accountid:712020:1dc09cac-8405-4059-a3b9-33f7c34affa8]) on what systemd-related metrics – either whether it might be useful for customers, or whether even support folks would be using them when troubleshooting customer issues.
* *Product Management:* Align with [~accountid:70121:02ceacb5-61bd-4604-a413-0001bd8c8bc7] on product strategy and priority for this kind of enhancement.

*Expected Deliverables:* Findings and evaluation shared in this Jira. If it ends up to be a useful enhancement, an RFE Jira ticket is created in the PCP backlog, potentially with an Epic.

items.toString: Previously, when using the rsyslog omelasticsearch module to forward logs to an Elasticsearch server over TLS, there was no way to specify the TLS protocol version, cipher suite list, or key exchange group, making it impossible to enable post-quantum cryptography (PQC) for these connections. There are two issues. The volume keys uploaded in thread keyring are released only after the kernel structure holding the reference to the credentials is released.
